claim: Ctf4 tightly dimerizes CMG helicase with an extensive interface involving Psf2, Cdc45, and Sld5.
source: Here we show that Ctf4 tightly dimerizes CMG helicase, with an extensive interface involving Psf2, Cdc45, and Sld5.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM structural data showing the interface between Ctf4 and CMG components, as presented in the manuscript's results section.

claim: Ctf4 binds only one Pol α-primase.
source: Interestingly, Ctf4 binds only one Pol α-primase.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM structural analysis and biochemical experiments showing 1:1 stoichiometry between Ctf4 trimer and Pol α-primase.

claim: Ctf4 may have evolved as a trimer to organize two helicases and one Pol α-primase into a replication factory.
source: Thus, Ctf4 may have evolved as a trimer to organize two helicases and one Pol α-primase into a replication factory.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the structural data showing Ctf4 can bind two CMGs and one Pol α-primase.

claim: In the 2CMG–Ctf43–1Pol α-primase factory model, the two CMGs nearly face each other, placing the two lagging strands toward the center and two leading strands out the sides.
source: In the 2CMG–Ctf43–1Pol α-primase factory model, the two CMGs nearly face each other, placing the two lagging strands toward the center and two leading strands out the sides.
evidence: The claim is based on the cryo-EM structure of the 2CMG-Ctf43 complex showing the spatial arrangement of the two CMG helicases.

claim: The single Pol α-primase is centrally located and may prime both sister replisomes.
source: The single Pol α-primase is centrally located and may prime both sister replisomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural positioning of Pol α-primase in the factory model.

claim: The Ctf4-coupled-sister replisome model is consistent with cellular microscopy studies revealing two sister forks of an origin remain attached and are pushed forward from a protein platform.
source: The Ctf4-coupled-sister replisome model is consistent with cellular microscopy studies revealing two sister forks of an origin remain attached and are pushed forward from a protein platform.
evidence: The claim draws on published cellular microscopy studies to support the proposed model.

claim: The replication factory model may facilitate parental nucleosome transfer during replication.
source: The replication factory model may facilitate parental nucleosome transfer during replication.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the structural model and known functions of Ctf4 in nucleosome transfer.

claim: Replication in eukaryotes utilizes CMG helicase (Cdc45−Mcm2-7−GINS) (Ilves et al., 2010; Moyer et al., 2006; Costa et al., 2011).
source: Replication in eukaryotes utilizes CMG helicase (Cdc45−Mcm2-7−GINS) (Ilves et al., 2010; Moyer et al., 2006; Costa et al., 2011)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Replication in eukaryotes is performed in localized foci in nuclei that contain 10–100 replication forks (Falaschi, 2000; Kitamura et al., 2006).
source: Replication in eukaryotes is performed in localized foci in nuclei that contain 10–100 replication forks (Falaschi, 2000; Kitamura et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Recent super resolution microscopy has resolved these foci into single replicon factories from bidirectional origins (Chagin et al., 2016; Saner et al., 2013).
source: Recent super resolution microscopy has resolved these foci into single replicon factories from bidirectional origins (Chagin et al., 2016; Saner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Nuclear foci in the budding yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisae, most often contain only single replicon factories having two replication forks, although some foci consist of more than two replication forks (Saner et al., 2013).
source: Nuclear foci in the budding yeast, Saccharomyces cerevisae, most often contain only single replicon factories having two replication forks, although some foci consist of more than two replication forks (Saner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a cited reference.

claim: Several studies demonstrate that sister replication forks remain together during S phase (Conti et al., 2007; Falaschi, 2000; Ligasová et al., 2009; Natsume and Tanaka, 2010).
source: several studies demonstrate that sister replication forks remain together during S phase (Conti et al., 2007; Falaschi, 2000; Ligasová et al., 2009; Natsume and Tanaka, 2010)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Sister double-strand (ds) DNA products are extruded in loops directed away from a replication protein scaffold (Gillespie and Blow, 2010; Saner et al., 2013).
source: sister double-strand (ds) DNA products are extruded in loops directed away from a replication protein scaffold (Gillespie and Blow, 2010; Saner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Ctf4 (Chromosome Transmission Fidelity 4) is a homo-trimer (Ctf43) that connects Pol α-primase and CMG helicase (Gambus et al., 2009; Miles and Formosa, 1992; Simon et al., 2014; Tanaka et al., 2009).
source: Ctf4 (Chromosome Transmission Fidelity 4) is a homo-trimer (Ctf43) that connects Pol α-primase and CMG helicase (Gambus et al., 2009; Miles and Formosa, 1992; Simon et al., 2014; Tanaka et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Previous EM studies reveal that Ctf43−Pol α-primase resides on the opposite side of CMG from the leading strand DNA polymerase (Pol) ε in an individual replisome (Sun et al., 2015).
source: Previous EM studies reveal that Ctf43−Pol α-primase resides on the opposite side of CMG from the leading strand DNA polymerase (Pol) ε in an individual replisome (Sun et al., 2015)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a cited reference.

claim: Ctf4 also transiently binds Dna2, Dpb2, Tof2 and Chl1, and thus Ctf4 is proposed to be a dynamic hub (Villa et al., 2016; Samora et al., 2016).
source: Ctf4 also transiently binds Dna2, Dpb2, Tof2 and Chl1, and thus Ctf4 is proposed to be a dynamic hub (Villa et al., 2016; Samora et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Dynamic interaction enables multiple factors binding through time-sharing on Ctf4 and occurs through a conserved Ctf4-Interaction Peptide (CIP) motif (Kilkenny et al., 2017; Samora et al., 2016; Simon et al., 2014; Villa et al., 2016).
source: Dynamic interaction enables multiple factors binding through time-sharing on Ctf4 and occurs through a conserved Ctf4-Interaction Peptide (CIP) motif (Kilkenny et al., 2017; Samora et al., 2016; Simon et al., 2014; Villa et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: The structures of the C-half of Ctf4 and its human orthologue AND1 reveal a disc-shaped constitutive trimer via the β-propeller domains on the N-terminal face (N-face) with the three C-terminal helical domains interacting with up to three CIP peptides on the C-face (Kilkenny et al., 2017; Simon et al., 2014).
source: The structures of the C-half of Ctf4 and its human orthologue AND1 reveal a disc-shaped constitutive trimer via the β-propeller domains on the N-terminal face (N-face) with the three C-terminal helical domains interacting with up to three CIP peptides on the C-face (Kilkenny et al., 2017; Simon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: Ctf4 mutants that disrupt connection to CMG are deficient in transfer of parental nucleosomes to the lagging strand daughter duplex, with implications for a role in epigenetic inheritance during development (Gan et al., 2018).
source: Ctf4 mutants that disrupt connection to CMG are deficient in transfer of parental nucleosomes to the lagging strand daughter duplex, with implications for a role in epigenetic inheritance during development (Gan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a cited reference.

claim: In human, AND1 (hCtf4) also binds CMG and is important for replication progression and DNA repair (Kang et al., 2013; Abe et al., 2018; Williams and McIntosh, 2002; Yoshizawa-Sugata and Masai, 2009).
source: In human, AND1 (hCtf4) also binds CMG and is important for replication progression and DNA repair (Kang et al., 2013; Abe et al., 2018; Williams and McIntosh, 2002; Yoshizawa-Sugata and Masai, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by cited references.

claim: CMG binding to Ctf43 was readily apparent in glycerol gradient sedimentation experiments.
source: CMG binding to Ctf43 was also readily apparent (compare panels c and g with panel e).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The CMG–Ctf43 complex migrated heavier than CMG–Pol ε in glycerol gradients.
source: It was initially surprising that the CMG–Ctf43 complex migrated heavier than CMG–Pol ε, even though Ctf43 is not quite as large as Pol ε
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data from glycerol gradient sedimentation.

claim: A complex of CMG–Ctf43 eluted at > 400 mM NaCl from a MonoQ ion exchange column.
source: To study the CMG–Ctf43 complex further we mixed Ctf43 and CMG and applied it to a MonoQ ion exchange column; a complex of CMG–Ctf43 eluted at > 400 mM NaCl (Figure 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2a.

claim: CMG−Ctf43 is a stable complex.
source: This result indicated CMG−Ctf43 is a stable complex, and is not loose, consistent wth an apparent tighter interaction of GINS complex to Ctf43 compared to the CIP peptide of Sld5 (Simon et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by ion exchange chromatography data and comparison to published work.

claim: The MonoQ isolated CMG–Ctf43 complex was stable to size-exclusion chromatography (SEC).
source: The MonoQ isolated CMG–Ctf43 complex was also stable to size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) (Figure 2b).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: CMG is tightly bound and highly stable on the Ctf43 hub.
source: We conclude that CMG is tightly bound and highly stable on the Ctf43 hub.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the chromatography experiments showing stable complex formation.

claim: Density scans of fractions within the SEC elution profile indicated a heterogeneous mixture of CMG–Ctf43 complexes, with CMG:Ctf43 ratios ranging from 3:1 to 1:1.
source: Density scans of fractions within the SEC elution profile indicated a heterogeneous mixture of CMG–Ctf43 complexes, with CMG:Ctf43 ratios ranging from 3:1 to 1:1.
evidence: The claim is supported by densitometry analysis of gel fractions.

claim: More than one CMG can bind Ctf43.
source: We therefore examined different fractions by cryo-EM and found that indeed, more than one CMG can bind Ctf43, as described below.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM analysis of different fractions.

claim: The structure of the 1CMG–Ctf43 complex was determined by cryo-EM to 3.9 Å resolution.
source: To investigate the structural basis underlying the strength of the CMG–Ctf43 complexes, we determined the structure of the 1CMG–Ctf43 complex by cryo-EM to 3.9 Å resolution.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM data and resolution determination.

claim: The C-tier AAA+ ring of Mcm2-7 is highly dynamic.
source: In agreement with previous structural studies of CMG (Abid Ali et al., 2016; Yuan et al., 2016), the C-tier AAA+ ring of Mcm2-7 is highly dynamic.
evidence: This is an observation consistent with previous structural studies.

claim: By excluding the C-tier AAA+ region in 3D refinement, the 3D map of 1CMG–Ctf43 was improved to 3.8 Å resolution.
source: By excluding this region in 3D refinement, we improved the 3D map of 1CMG–Ctf43 to 3.8 Å resolution (Figure 3a–c, Table 1, Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM data processing methods and results.

claim: The overall architecture reveals an extensive interface between the helicase and Ctf43, amounting to 1706 Å2 of buried area.
source: The overall architecture reveals an extensive interface between the helicase and Ctf43, amounting to 1706 Å2 of buried area
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis of the cryo-EM model.

claim: The interface between CMG and Ctf43 (1706 Å2) is larger than the stable contact between Cdc45 and Mcm2-7 (1182 Å2) and between GINS and Mcm2-7 (1583 Å2).
source: larger than the stable contact between Cdc45 and Mcm2-7 (1182 Å2) and between GINS and Mcm2-7 (1583 Å2), explaining the stability of the CMG–Ctf43 complex.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis comparing buried surface areas.

claim: There is a wide gap between Ctf4 and the Sld5 subunit of CMG that contains the CIP peptide.
source: Interestingly, there is a wide gap between Ctf4 and the Sld5 subunit of CMG that contains the CIP peptide (Figure 4a).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural observation in the cryo-EM model.

claim: There are three interfaces between CMG and Ctf43, involving three different subunits of CMG with one protomer of Ctf43.
source: There are three interfaces between CMG and Ctf43, involving three different subunits of CMG with one protomer of Ctf43 (Figure 4c,d,e; Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis shown in figures.

claim: The two major interfaces are between the β-propeller region of Ctf4 and both the Cdc45 subunit of CMG and the Psf2 subunit in the GINS complex of CMG.
source: The two major interfaces are between the β-propeller region of Ctf4 and both the Cdc45 subunit of CMG (Figure 4c) and the Psf2 subunit in the GINS complex of CMG (Figure 4d); these interfaces were previously uncharacterized.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis of the cryo-EM model.

claim: The interactions between Cdc45 and the Ctf4 propeller are largely electrostatic, involving several salt bridges and hydrogen bonds.
source: The interactions between Cdc45 and the Ctf4 propeller are largely electrostatic, involving several salt bridges and hydrogen bonds.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis of the interface.

claim: A loop connecting strands β1 and β2 of Psf2, disordered in the CMG structure in the absence of Ctf43, inserts into two blades of the β-propeller and becomes ordered by forming multiple interactions.
source: Furthermore, a loop connecting strands β1 and β2 of Psf2, disordered in the CMG structure in the absence of Ctf43 (Yuan et al., 2016), inserts into two blades of the β-propeller and becomes ordered by forming multiple interactions (Figure 4d).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural comparison with previous CMG structures.

claim: The interface between Psf2 and Ctf4 involves H-bonds between Psf2 residues Arg34 and Lys36 with Ctf4 residues Asn850 and Tyr848, respectively, as well as hydrophobic interaction among Ctf4 residues Phe518, Leu770, and Pro771 and Psf2 residues Ile27, Phe28, and Pro29.
source: The interface between Psf2 and Ctf4 involves H-bonds between Psf2 residues Arg34 and Lys36 with Ctf4 residues Asn850 and Tyr848, respectively, as well as hydrophobic interaction among Ctf4 residues Phe518, Leu770, and Pro771 and Psf2 residues Ile27, Phe28, and Pro29.
evidence: The claim is supported by detailed structural analysis of the interface.

claim: The main Ctf4-contacting regions of Cdc45 and Psf2 are well conserved across evolution.
source: As expected, the main Ctf4-contacting regions of Cdc45, Psf2 are well conserved across evolution (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by sequence conservation analysis shown in the figure supplement.

claim: The N-terminal residues 3–15 of Sld5 form a short helix that bundles with the helical domain of Ctf4, primarily via a hydrophobic interface.
source: The previously-identified interaction between Ctf4 and the CIP peptide in the Sld5 subunit (Simon et al., 2014) of the GINS complex is actually a minor interaction site in which the N-terminal residues 3–15 of Sld5 form a short helix that bundles with the helical domain of Ctf4, primarily via a hydrophobic interface (Figure 4e).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis of the Sld5-Ctf4 interface.

claim: An intervening long peptide (aa 16–53) of Sld5 is disordered.
source: An intervening long peptide (aa 16–53) of Sld5 is disordered.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural observation in the cryo-EM model.

claim: The long flexible linker to the CIP peptide of Sld5 may explain why the CIP peptide of Sld5 is not required to observe CMG binding to Ctf4 in cells.
source: This long flexible linker to the CIP peptide of Sld5 may explain why the CIP peptide of Sld5 is not required to observe CMG binding to Ctf4 in cells, predicting a second tethering point between CMG and Ctf4 (Simon et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observation and comparison to cellular studies.

claim: The Psf2 and Cdc45 extensive interfaces explain the stable association between Ctf4 and CMG.
source: Therefore the Psf2 and Cdc45 extensive interfaces explain the stable association between Ctf4 and CMG.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural analysis of the interfaces.

claim: Cryo-EM 2D averages of two CMGs bound to Ctf43 show the CMGs are held rigidly.
source: Cryo-EM 2D averages of two CMGs bound to Ctf43 show the CMGs are held rigidly, consistent with their stable binding to Ctf43 (Figure 5a).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM 2D class averages.

claim: Each CMG interacts with only one protomer of Ctf43, and the CMG contact is limited to one side of the Ctf43 triangle related by 120°.
source: The 3D reconstruction shows each CMG interacts with only one protomer of Ctf43, and the CMG contact is limited to one side of the Ctf43 triangle related by 120° (Figure 5b).
evidence: The claim is supported by 3D reconstruction of the 2CMG-Ctf43 complex.

claim: The structure of 2CMG–Ctf43 shows that the large CMGs do not sterically obstruct one another.
source: However the structure of 2CMG–Ctf43 shows that the large CMGs do not sterically obstruct one another.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis of the 2CMG-Ctf43 complex.

claim: One Ctf43 may organize up to three CMGs.
source: Therefore, one Ctf43 may organize up to three CMGs.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observation that CMGs do not clash.

claim: 2D class averages show two or three CMGs per Ctf43, related by the three-fold axis of Ctf43.
source: Indeed, we observed 2D class averages that show two or three CMGs per Ctf43, related by the three-fold axis of Ctf43 (Figure 5a, Figure 5—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM 2D class averages.

claim: The cryo-EM 3D map of the 2CMG–Ctf43 complex was determined at 5.8 Å resolution.
source: We determined the cryo-EM 3D maps of the 2CMG–Ctf43 complex at 5.8 Å resolution (Figure 5b, Figure 5—figure supplement 1, Video 2)
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM data and resolution determination.

claim: The cryo-EM 3D map of the 3CMG–Ctf43 complex was determined at 7.0 Å resolution.
source: and the 3CMG–Ctf43 complex at 7.0 Å (Figure 5—figure supplement 2), respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM data and resolution determination.

claim: The interactions between individual CMG helicases and their respective partner Ctf4 protomers in both 2CMG–Ctf43 and 3CMG–Ctf43 complexes are virtually identical, the same as in the 1CMG–Ctf43 complex.
source: The interactions between individual CMG helicases and their respective partner Ctf4 protomers in both 2CMG–Ctf43 and 3CMG–Ctf43 complexes are virtually identical, the same as in the 1CMG–Ctf43 complex described above, consistent with no steric clash between the CMGs.
evidence: The claim is supported by comparison of the three different complex structures.

claim: The two CMGs are held on the same side − the top side, or the N-face of the disc-shaped Ctf43.
source: The key insight from the 2CMG–Ctf43 structure is that the two CMGs are held on the same side − the top side, or the N-face of the disc-shaped Ctf43 when the structure is viewed from the side of the Ctf43 disk (Figure 5b).
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis of the 2CMG-Ctf43 complex.

claim: The two N-tier rings of the Mcm2-7 hexamers approximately face one another at an angle of 120°.
source: Hence, the two N-tier rings of the Mcm2-7 hexamers – where the dsDNAs approach for dsDNA unwinding (Georgescu et al., 2017; Douglas et al., 2018) – approximately face one another at an angle of 120°
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis and cited references about CMG function.

claim: The C-tier motor rings of the two CMGs face outwards and away from each other.
source: and the C-tier motor rings of the two CMGs, where the leading strand Pol ε's bind (Sun et al., 2015), face outwards and away from each other.
evidence: The claim is supported by structural analysis and cited reference about Pol ε binding.

claim: The interaction of Ctf43 to Pol α-primase was too loose to isolate a complex for cryo-EM analysis.
source: We wished to understand the basis of this stoichiometry but the interaction of Ctf43 to Pol α-primase was too loose to isolate a complex for cryo-EM analysis, consistent with the dynamic hub model of Ctf43 (Simon et al., 2014; Villa et al., 2016).
evidence: This is an experimental observation consistent with the dynamic hub model.

claim: Pol α-primase was flexible when frozen in vitreous ice and did not generate well-defined 2D class averages.
source: We first examined Pol α-primase alone and found Pol α-primase was flexible when frozen in vitreous ice, and did not generate well-defined 2D class averages.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from cryo-EM analysis.

claim: Under negative-stain EM conditions, Pol α-primase was sufficiently stabilized on carbon film to yield a bi-lobed shape with the two lobes ~ 120 Å apart.
source: But under negative-stain EM conditions, Pol α-primase was sufficiently stabilized on carbon film to yield a bi-lobed shape with the two lobes ~ 120 Å apart (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from negative-stain EM.

claim: The architecture of Pol α-primase is essentially the same as a previous negative-stain EM study, in which one lobe is assigned to the catalytic NTD of Pol1 (Pol1-NTD) and the other lobe to the CTD of Pol1, plus the B-subunit and the L- and S-subunits of the primase (Núñez-Ramírez et al., 2011).
source: This architecture is essentially the same as a previous negative-stain EM study, in which one lobe is assigned to the catalytic NTD of Pol1 (Pol1-NTD) and the other lobe to the CTD of Pol1, plus the B-subunit and the L- and S-subunits of the primase (Núñez-Ramírez et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a comparison to a previous structural study.

claim: Cryo-EM 2D class averages of a 1:1 molar ratio mixture of Ctf43 and Pol α-primase yielded a structure comprised of Ctf43 bound to one catalytic Pol1-NTD of Pol α-primase.
source: Cryo-EM 2D class averages of a 1:1 molar ratio mixture of Ctf43 and Pol α-primase yielded a structure comprised of Ctf43 bound to one catalytic Pol1-NTD of Pol α-primase (Figure 6c, Figure 6—figure supplement 1, Table 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM 2D class averages.

claim: Increasing the Pol α:Ctf43 ratio to 3:1 did not change the 1:1 binding with Ctf43.
source: Increasing the Pol α:Ctf43 ratio to 3:1 did not change the 1:1 binding with Ctf43 (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by cryo-EM analysis at different molar ratios.

claim: The presence of the Pol lobe, but absence of the primase lobe in the 2D class averages is consistent with previous studies showing a high degree of flexibility between the primase and polymerase lobes (Baranovskiy and Tahirov, 2017; Núñez-Ramírez et al., 2011; Perera et al., 2013).
source: The presence of the Pol lobe, but absence of the primase lobe in the 2D class averages is consistent with previous studies showing a high degree of flexibility between the primase and polymerase lobes (Baranovskiy and Tahirov, 2017; Núñez-Ramírez et al., 2011; Perera et al., 2013).
evidence: This is an observation consistent with previous structural studies.

claim: The 2D averages reveal two contacts between Ctf43 and Pol1-NTD, but only one of the two contacts is visible in the 3D map.
source: The 2D averages reveal two contacts between Ctf43 and Pol1-NTD, but only one of the two contacts is visible in the 3D map (Figure 6c–d).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing 2D and 3D reconstructions.

claim: The interactions between Ctf43 and Pol1-NTD must be weak and flexible, with one contact becoming averaged out in 3D reconstructions, accounting for the low 12 Å resolution of the 3D map.
source: These interactions must be weak and flexible, with one contact becoming averaged out in 3D reconstructions, and accounting for the low 12 Å resolution of the 3D map.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural observations and resolution.

claim: The crystal structures of Ctf43 and Pol1-NTD complexed with a primed DNA-dNTP fit well as two separate rigid-bodies in the upper and lower densities of the Ctf43–apo Pol1-NTD 3D map.
source: The crystal structures of Ctf43 and Pol1-NTD complexed with a primed DNA-dNTP fit well as two separate rigid-bodies in the upper and lower densities of the Ctf43–apo Pol1-NTD 3D map, respectively.
evidence: The claim is supported by rigid-body docking of crystal structures into the cryo-EM map.

claim: The docking suggests that the primer-template duplex exits the Pol1-NTD from the bottom face.
source: The docking suggests that the primer-template duplex exits the Pol1-NTD from the bottom face (Figure 6d, Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference based on the docking of crystal structures.

claim: Use of a three-fold excess of Pol α-primase to Ctf43 did not provide more than one molecule of Pol α-primase bound to the Ctf4 trimer.
source: The fact that use of a three-fold excess of Pol α-primase to Ctf43 did not provide more than one molecule of Pol α-primase bound to the Ctf4 trimer (Figure 6—figure supplement 2), is consistent with the previous observations (Simon et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data and comparison to previous work.

claim: The Pol1-NTD occupies most of the bottom C-face of Ctf43, appearing to sterically occlude additional molecules of Pol α-primase.
source: The Pol1-NTD occupies most of the bottom C-face of Ctf43 (Figure 6d, Figure 6—figure supplement 1), appearing to sterically occlude additional molecules of Pol α-primase and thus explaining the single Pol α-primase-to-Ctf43 stoichiometry.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural model explaining the stoichiometry.

claim: A mixture of CMG+Ctf43 with DNA Pol α-primase and Pol ε produced a large super-complex that surpassed the size of CMG–Ctf43 and the Pol ε-CMG complexes.
source: To investigate complex formation among CMG, Ctf43 and DNA polymerases, we analyzed by densitometry the sedimentation analyses of a mixture of CMG+Ctf43 with DNA Pol α-primase and Pol ε. This protein mixture produced a large super-complex that surpassed the size of CMG–Ctf43 and the Pol ε-CMG complexes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by glycerol gradient sedimentation analysis.

claim: The bulk of excess Ctf43 is excluded from the large complex suggesting some type of cooperative assembly.
source: Interestingly, the bulk of excess Ctf43 is excluded from the large complex suggesting some type of cooperative assembly.
evidence: This is an observation from the sedimentation analysis suggesting cooperativity.

claim: Gel scans indicate a stoichiometry of two CMG–Pol ε, one Ctf43, one Pol α-primase.
source: Gel scans indicate a stoichiometry of two CMG–Pol ε, one Ctf43, one Pol α-primase (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), although we can't exclude a possible mixture of complexes.
evidence: The claim is supported by densitometry analysis of gel fractions.

claim: Upon mixing CMG+Ctf43+Pol α-primase a 2CMG–1Ctf43–1Pol α-primase complex was observed by negative stain EM.
source: Upon mixing CMG+Ctf43+Pol α-primase we observed a 2CMG–1Ctf43–1Pol α-primase complex by negative stain EM (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by negative stain EM observations.

claim: Pull-down assays using immobilized Ctf43 showed an 8-fold increase of Pol α-primase retained on Ctf43 when CMG was present.
source: Pull-down assays using immobilized Ctf43 showed an 8-fold increase of Pol α-primase retained on Ctf43 when CMG was present
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down assay data.

claim: More CMG bound to Ctf43 when Pol α-primase was present, suggesting cooperativity.
source: and conversely, more CMG bound to Ctf43 when Pol α-primase was present, suggesting cooperativity (Figure 7a).
evidence: The claim is supported by pull-down assay data.

claim: The spontaneous and cooperative assembly of the 2CMG–Pol ε–1Ctf43–1Pol α-primase complex in vitro suggests that the complex may also form in cells.
source: The spontaneous and cooperative assembly of this complex in vitro suggests that the complex may also form in cells and possibly underlies the observations that sister replisomes are held together in cells (Chagin et al., 2016; Saner et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the in vitro observations and cited cellular studies.

claim: CMG helicase activity is slightly stimulated by Ctf4 compared to CMG alone.
source: The results demonstrate that CMG helicase activity is slightly stimulated by Ctf4 compared to CMG alone (Figure 7b).
evidence: The claim is supported by helicase assay data.

claim: Stimulation of CMG by Ctf4 was observed in an earlier study using human CMG and Ctf4 (Kang et al., 2013).
source: Stimulation of CMG by Ctf4 was observed in an earlier study using human CMG and Ctf4 (Kang et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a reference to a previous study showing similar results.

claim: CMG retains helicase activity while multimerized by Ctf43.
source: Overall, we conclude CMG retains helicase activity while multimerized by Ctf43.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the helicase assay data.

claim: Comparison of CMG+Pol α-primase with CMG+Ctf43+Pol α-primase showed that CMG retained full replication activity while multimerized by Ctf43.
